page: Amazon Web Services x1e.32xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance running on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by four Intel Xeon E7-8880 v3 processors operating at 2.3 GHz, supplying 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading. Designed for memory-bound workloads, the instance delivers an exceptional 3904.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 30.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include 3840 GB of bundled local SSD storage, 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and instruction extensions such as AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, though modern AVX-512 extensions are absent.

Benchmark results highlight the extreme focus on aggregate capacity and parallel execution over single-threaded speed. The older Haswell-EX microarchitecture yields poor single-core performance, scoring in the bottom 10 percent in Geekbench and stress-ng tests. However, the 128 vCPUs provide strong aggregate throughput, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 49221.05 and sustained memory bandwidth exceeding 201 GB/sec for uncached read operations. Redis operations reach 60.25 million operations per second, supported by massive RAM capacity and multi-threaded decompression handling.

The primary tradeoff of the x1e.32xlarge lies in its older architecture, where single-threaded execution and per-core efficiency are lower compared to newer generations. In exchange, it offers unmatched memory capacity per instance without partitioning data across distributed nodes. The bundled 3840 GB local SSD storage ensures rapid local scratch space and logging throughput. The instance is suited for large-scale in-memory databases like SAP HANA, massive Apache Spark caching tiers, electronic design automation (EDA), and complex enterprise in-memory analytics.
description: Amazon Web Services x1e.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance designed for enterprise applications requiring vast memory footprints. Based on the x86_64 architecture and the Xen hypervisor, it features 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores using Intel Xeon E7-8880 v3 processors clocked at 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 3904.0 GB of system memory, bundled 3840 GB local SSD storage, and a 25 Gbps network interface without dedicated GPUs. Benchmark data demonstrates strong multi-core processing with a PassMark CPU score of 49221.05 and high aggregate memory read bandwidth of 201.38 GB/sec. Conversely, single-thread performance ranks in the bottom 10 percent due to older core architecture. With roughly 30.5 GB of RAM per vCPU, x1e.32xlarge serves workloads such as enterprise in-memory computing, SAP HANA deployments, massive memory caching, and large-scale data analytics pipelines.
